nh_new_wave.blurb: A compact, sun-catching cliff high on Rattlesnake Mountain at Rumney, mostly bolted sport lines with a pair of trad options. The 22 routes run from the 5.6 range through the 5.13s, with the heaviest cluster in the low 5.11s to 5.12s, so it suits strong leaders more than first-timers. The left side has paler, mica-flecked rock with good features, while the right turns dark, crimpy and technical. Everything is packed onto one narrow ledge, so elbow room is scarce when it fills up, and the drop below is long, which makes careful handling of gear and pets important.

nh_wonder_wall.blurb: The biggest steep wall in the Conway valley, forming part of the South Buttress end of Whitehorse Ledge. Where the rest of the ledge is known for friction slabs, this is vertical, pumpy trad climbing, mostly crimpy face moves with some cracks, corners, flakes and roofs. Most of the 22 routes fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with a few easier lines. Two broad ledges divide the cliff into lower and upper halves; the lower routes are single pitches, while the upper wall sits roughly 250 feet up and takes a longer, more committing approach with some scrambling.

nh_4_wonderland_wall.blurb: The right-hand end of Longstack Precipice, above the Lakes Region east of Lake Winnipesaukee. All 22 routes are trad, many of them two pitches, spanning roughly 5.5 up to the low 5.11s with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, which makes it a solid choice for moderate leaders. Climbs start along a set of natural rock steps that lead up toward the end of the cliff. The wider crag is regarded as one of the quicker-drying walls in the state, and a standard rack to about a number 3 handles most lines.

nh_y_crag.blurb: The largest crag in the Russell Forest group near Woodstock, in the schist country west of the Kancamagus. It is a complex, many-faceted cliff holding 22 routes, mostly bolted sport with five trad lines, and offers an unusually wide spread: a handful of easy climbs, a good number of 5.9 to 5.10 lines, and a strong dose of 5.11 and 5.12 testpieces. Some routes are multi-pitch. It is the farthest of the main crags in the forest from the road, but the walk-in is only about ten to fifteen minutes on a trail marked with blue ribbons, steep and winding near the top.

nh_northeastern_crags_the.blurb: A string of partly developed granite cliffs to the right of the main wall at Greens Cliff in the White Mountains, looking out over the Sawyer Pond basin. All 22 routes are trad, mostly crack climbs from fingers to hands with a few chimneys, on walls slightly past vertical with some overhangs. Most are one or two pitches, with a third or fourth sometimes set back above. Grades cluster at 5.9 and 5.10, with a few harder lines. Shade arrives early in the day, making these a cooler summer alternative to the sunny main wall, though late fall can feel chilly. The hike in is the shortest of anywhere at Greens, well under an hour.
